text: AIF is a central financing facility - not a direct cash-transfer scheme - for building post-harvest and community-farming infrastructure: warehouses, cold chains, primary processing units, custom hiring centres for farm machinery, and similar projects. Launched in August 2020 under Aatmanirbhar Bharat with a Rs 1 lakh crore corpus, running through FY2032. Loans up to Rs 2 crore per project get a 3% per annum interest subvention for up to 7 years (capped so the effective rate doesn't exceed about 9%), plus credit-guarantee coverage under CGTMSE so no collateral is required up to that limit - the government pays the guarantee fee. There is no direct cash subsidy; the benefit is entirely through cheaper borrowing.

Farmers, FPOs, cooperatives, SHGs, agri-entrepreneurs, start-ups, and state agencies can all apply for eligible post-harvest/community-farming infrastructure projects. Private-sector applicants (individual farmers, entrepreneurs, start-ups) are capped at 25 projects each; state agencies and federations of cooperatives/FPOs/SHGs have no such cap. A minimum 10% borrower contribution to project cost is required. Applications go through the AIF Management Information System portal, with participating banks and NABARD handling disbursement.

interest-subvention rate, loan cap, and CGTMSE guarantee are corroborated by the scheme's own official FAQ page (agriinfra.dac.gov.in) plus multiple state agriculture department pages - among the strongest-sourced entries in this knowledge base. This is an infrastructure LOAN facility, not an income-support payment - do not conflate with PM-KISAN or state cash-transfer schemes when explaining it to a farmer.

scheme_name: Annadata Sukhibhava (Andhra Pradesh) - successor to YSR Rythu Bharosa
text: Andhra Pradesh's state-level income-support top-up for farmers, layered on top of central PM-KISAN. Multiple, partially conflicting sources describe a transition: the scheme was run as 'YSR Rythu Bharosa' (Rs 13,500/year per farmer family, in 3 instalments, inclusive of the Rs 6,000 PM-KISAN central share) from October 2019 until Andhra Pradesh's 2024 change of state government. It has since been relaunched as 'Annadata Sukhibhava' by the current state government, reported in several sources at a flat Rs 20,000/year per farmer family (again inclusive of the PM-KISAN Rs 6,000 central share) - but exact current disbursement status and installment schedule vary by source and should be verified on the official portal before being quoted as fact to a farmer.

scheme_name: Annadata Sukhibhava (Andhra Pradesh) - successor to YSR Rythu Bharosa
text: Historically (YSR Rythu Bharosa): land-owning farmer families of any holding size, plus landless tenant farmers, ROFR/D-Patta/inam/temple-land cultivators, especially from SC/ST/BC/minority categories, with PM-KISAN enrolment generally treated as automatic state-scheme eligibility too. Exclusions historically included sitting/former Ministers, MPs, MLAs, and MLCs (though other elected representatives were not excluded) - this is a NARROWER exclusion list than PM-KISAN's central rules, so a person excluded from PM-KISAN is not automatically excluded from this state scheme, and vice versa. Whether these exact eligibility terms carried over unchanged into Annadata Sukhibhava is not yet confirmed in this knowledge base.

scheme_name: Annadata Sukhibhava (Andhra Pradesh) - successor to YSR Rythu Bharosa
text: LOWER than the other entries in this knowledge base. The 2024-25 scheme rename/transition is corroborated across several independent secondary sources, but they partially disagree on exact current benefit amounts and disbursement timelines - a genuine sign of an administrative transition still settling, not a research gap on our end. The eligibility engine should treat any Annadata Sukhibhava query as Insufficient information pending direct confirmation from ysrrythubharosa.ap.gov.in or its successor portal, even though PM-KISAN (a related but legally separate central scheme) can still be checked normally.

The Kisan Credit Card gives farmers a revolving credit line for crop production and allied activities (animal husbandry, dairy, fisheries), plus post-harvest and working-capital needs. Short-term loans up to a government-set threshold (being raised from Rs 3 lakh to Rs 5 lakh per the Union Budget 2025-26) carry a concessional 7% per annum interest rate under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme; farmers who repay on time can receive a further Prompt Repayment Incentive that brings the effective rate down to around 4%. Loans up to roughly Rs 1.6-2 lakh are collateral-free. The card is valid for five years, with the limit reviewed and increased annually.

Owner-cultivators, tenant farmers, oral lessees, and sharecroppers can all apply, individually or jointly, at any scheduled commercial bank, RRB, cooperative bank, or small finance bank. Aadhaar linkage is mandatory to receive the interest subvention.

interest rate, subvention structure, and the 2025-26 Budget increase to Rs 5 lakh are corroborated by an official PIB press release and the Kisan Rin Portal (fasalrin.gov.in) - the two strongest sources in this batch's search.

PM-KISAN is a central income-support scheme that pays landholding farmer families a fixed Rs 6,000 per year, split into three equal instalments of Rs 2,000 each, credited directly to an Aadhaar-linked bank account. A 'farmer family' is defined as husband, wife, and minor children who jointly own cultivable agricultural land, as recorded in their state's official land records. Registration happens on the pmkisan.gov.in portal or through Common Service Centres, and requires Aadhaar-based e-KYC before instalments are released.

The scheme excludes several categories even if they own farmland: institutional landholders; serving or retired government employees and PSU officers above Group D/Class IV level; pensioners drawing Rs 10,000 or more per month (Group D/Class IV exempted from this exclusion); income-tax payers; and registered professionals such as doctors, engineers, lawyers, chartered accountants, and architects who are in active practice. Current or former holders of constitutional posts, ministers, MPs, MLAs, and similar elected office-holders are also excluded.

well-corroborated across multiple secondary sources; benefit amount and instalment structure independently confirmed; exact current-cycle dates and any 2026 policy tweaks should still be checked against pmkisan.gov.in directly before being quoted to a farmer.

PMFBY is India's crop insurance scheme, protecting farmers against yield loss from natural calamities, pests, and disease, across the full crop cycle from prevented sowing through post-harvest damage. Farmers pay a small, fixed share of the premium - about 2% of the sum insured for Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi crops, and 5% for commercial/horticultural crops - and the Central and State governments jointly subsidize the remaining actuarial premium. Only crops and areas officially notified by the relevant State Government are covered, so coverage varies by state and season. Enrolment has been voluntary since 2020 (it was compulsory for Kisan Credit Card loanees before that).

Any farmer - owner-cultivator or tenant/sharecropper with an insurable interest in a notified crop in a notified area - can enrol, via a bank, an empanelled insurer, a Common Service Centre, or the pmfby.gov.in portal. Localized damage (hailstorm, landslide, flooding, etc.) must be reported within 72 hours of the event through the Crop Insurance app or helpline for the claim to be considered.

premium percentages and the 72-hour reporting rule are consistent across many sources; exact notified-crop lists are state- and season-specific and are NOT in this knowledge base yet - the eligibility engine must treat 'is my crop covered' as insufficient_information until state notification data is sourced (Category C/D, next batch).
